profileSections.summary: Monterey Pine is an introduced plantation tree that Florabase records as alien and naturalised in parts of Western Australia; trees commonly reach about 30 to 40 metres.
profileSections.identifying_features: Leaves are borne in bundles of three and are about 8 to 15 centimetres long; the woody cones contain many scales and the seeds are winged.
profileSections.crown_form: Mature trees develop a broad, irregular conifer crown, while younger plantation trees are more conical.
profileSections.reproduction: Florabase records the species as monoecious, with winged seed and flowering mainly in September and October.
profileSections.habitat: Western Australian naturalisation is associated particularly with plantations and nearby disturbed or bushland environments.
profileSections.distribution: Records occur in the Avon Wheatbelt, Jarrah Forest, Swan Coastal Plain and Warren bioregions.
profileSections.fire_response: Fire generally kills mature trees but opens cones and releases seed; dense post-fire germination can follow.
profileSections.regional_status: Current in Florabase, not threatened and alien to Western Australia; native to coastal California and nearby islands.
profileSections.data_quality: Florabase profile 88 was curated into ArbotFlash on 17 June 2026.

profileSections.summary: Stone Pine is an introduced conifer recorded by Florabase as a tree to about 20 metres high and alien to Western Australia.
profileSections.identifying_features: Mature trees develop a broad, flat-topped umbrella or mushroom-shaped crown. Needles occur in pairs and are more than about 12 centimetres long.
profileSections.fruit_and_seed: The species produces woody cones and large seeds with only rudimentary wings; these are the edible pine nuts associated with Stone Pine.
profileSections.habitat: The Western Australian Florabase record notes white sand over clay on flats.
profileSections.distribution: Florabase records the species from the Esperance Plains, including the Recherche subregion.
profileSections.regional_status: Current in Florabase, not threatened and alien to Western Australia.
profileSections.media_note: The reviewed whole-form image was photographed in Doñana, Spain and demonstrates the mature umbrella-shaped crown in a Mediterranean landscape.
